title: Talking about the past
title_target: Dhèk cilik aku manggon ing désa
goal: Tell stories about the past without changing a single letter of the verb — using time words that stand on their own instead of past tense endings.
bekal: using *dhèk* and *kepungkur* to place events in the past
telling events in sequence with *nalika*, *banjur*, *sawisé kuwi*
telling *wis* (already) apart from *tau* (ever) and *biyèn* (in the past)

dialogs.title: Dialogue — Crita bocah désa
dialogs.intro: It's pouring with rain and everyone is stuck on the porch. Rini talks about her childhood in Klaten. A ngoko conversation, almost all in the past — notice that not one verb changes form.

lines.speaker: Rini:
lines.text: Dhèk cilik aku ora manggon ing kutha, Yan.
lines.id: When I was little I didn't live in the city, Yan.
lines.literal: when small I not live in city, Yan.

lines.speaker: Rini:
lines.text: Ing désa, cedhak sawah. Omahé simbah.
lines.id: In a village, near the rice fields. At my grandma's house.
lines.literal: in village, near rice-field. house-the grandma.

lines.speaker: Rini:
lines.text: Seneng. Saben soré aku dolan ing kali karo kanca-kanca.
lines.id: Fun. Every afternoon I played in the river with my friends.
lines.literal: happy. every afternoon I play in river with friend-friend.

lines.speaker: Dian:
lines.id: Didn't your grandma tell you off?

lines.speaker: Rini:
lines.text: Kerep. Nalika aku kelas telu, aku tiba ing kali, banjur lara seminggu.
lines.id: Often. When I was in third grade, I fell in the river, then I was ill for a week.
lines.literal: often. when I class three, I fall in river, then sick one-week.

lines.speaker: Dian:
lines.text: Wah. Sawisé kuwi isih dolan ing kali?
lines.id: Wow. After that did you still play in the river?
lines.literal: wow. after that still play in river?

lines.speaker: Rini:
lines.text: Ha ha, isih. Nanging ora tau ngomong marang simbah manèh.
lines.id: Ha ha, I did. But I never told my grandma again.
lines.literal: ha ha, still. but not ever say to grandma again.

lines.speaker: Dian:
lines.id: When did you move to the city?

lines.speaker: Rini:
lines.text: Telung taun kepungkur, nalika wiwit kuliah.
lines.id: Three years ago, when I started university.
lines.literal: three year ago, when start lecture.

lines.speaker: Rini:
lines.text: Kangen tenan. Nanging saiki wis kulina ing kéné.
lines.id: I really miss it. But now I'm used to it here.
lines.literal: miss truly. but now already used at here.

notes: **Dhèk** is a past-time marker placed before the time expression: *dhèk cilik* (when I was little), *dhèk wingi* (yesterday), *dhèk Senèn* (last Monday), *dhèk semana* (back then). The krama is *nalika* or *rikala*. English has no one-word equivalent — the closest is "back when".
**Kepungkur** means "ago, last" and comes **after** the time unit: *minggu kepungkur* (last week), *sasi kepungkur* (last month), *telung taun kepungkur* (three years ago). The krama is *kepengker*.
**Diseneni** = *di-* + *seneni* (to scold), "be scolded". The passive *di-*, which has appeared several times already, is fully explained two units from now — in unit 18.
**Tiba** means "to fall"; the krama is *dhawah*. If you know Indonesian, beware: there *tiba* means "to arrive". For "to arrive", Javanese uses *tekan*.
**Kangen** means "to miss, to long for" — Indonesian borrowed it from Javanese. The krama is also *kangen*; a more refined version is *kangen sanget*.
**Marang** means "to" (a person); the krama is *dhateng*. It marks the target of an action: *ngomong marang simbah* (say to grandma), *mènèhi marang kanca* (give to a friend).

grammars.title: The past without changing the verb
body: This is the most reassuring part of the whole course. Javanese **has no past tense**. The verb is exactly the same as the one you use for now; what puts an event in the past is the time words around it.
after: **Tell wis, tau, and biyèn apart.** *Aku wis mangan* = I've already eaten (today). *Aku wis tau mangan gudeg* = I've eaten gudeg before (at some point in my life). *Biyèn aku kerep mangan gudeg* = I used to eat gudeg often (an old habit that has stopped).

**The verb doesn't move at all.** *Aku mangan* can mean "I eat", "I'm eating", or "I ate (yesterday)" — it all depends on the time words around it. If there are none at all, the context of the conversation decides, and that is almost always enough.
**When in doubt, add a time word.** A sentence with one time word too many is never wrong in Javanese; a sentence with none can be misunderstood.

blocks.text: Javanese stories almost always use the same frame, and it covers everything you need at A1. You'll find it is much like the way you tell a story in English.

The most useful practice in this whole unit: tell the story of **your own yesterday** using the frame above, in just five sentences. If you can do it without stopping, you can already tell stories in Javanese.

blocks.title: Typical story openers
items: **Anu…** — a filler, like "um" or "what's-it". Used while you are looking for a word. You will hear it constantly, and using it actually makes you sound natural.
**Ngéné, lho** — "it's like this, see". Opens a long explanation.
**Jaréné** — "apparently, they say". Opens news heard from someone else: *jaréné udan gedhé ing Kaliurang*. The krama is *criyosipun*.
**Jebulé** — "it turned out". Opens the surprising part of a story: *jebulé HP-ku ana ing tas*. The krama is *jebulipun*.

sections.title: Verbs that often appear in stories

blocks.text: **Duka** hides a trap worth knowing now: in krama it means "angry" (of a respected person), but in conversation it is also very often used for **"I don't know"** — a polite form of *boten mangertos*. If someone answers your question with *duka*, they are saying "I'm not sure", not that they are angry.

items: ____ ésuk aku ketemu Rini ing kampus.

exercises.prompt: Put these into a story in order with *banjur* and *sawisé kuwi*.

items: When I was little I lived in a village.
Three years ago I moved to the city.
Yesterday I fell in the street.
I have never been to Bali.
It turned out my phone was in my bag.

exercises.prompt: **Review of Unit 14.** Cover Unit 14, then write these sentences in Javanese (krama).

answers: Aku tangi telat. — banjur mlayu nyang kampus. — Jebulé kuliahé wis wiwit. — mula aku ora éntuk mlebu. — Sawisé kuwi aku mulih manèh.
Dhèk cilik aku manggon ing désa. — Telung taun kepungkur aku pindhah nyang kutha. — Wingi aku tiba ing dalan. — Aku durung tau nyang Bali. — Jaréné wingi udan gedhé. — Jebulé HP-ku ana ing tas.
Kula sakit, Pak. — Sirah kula mumet. — Sampun ngunjuk jampi dèrèng? — Ndang saras, nggih. — Kula boten sakéca.
